reviewedFields.exceptionReason: The renewed curriculum confirms 90 of 180 EC. The examination components and credits for year two and the final phase of year three, including the thesis requirements, remain unconfirmed for September 2026 entrants.
reviewedFields.curriculumContext: The adopted regulations confirm 60 EC in year one and 30 EC of third-year minor study. The remaining 90 EC will be specified in the 2027–2028 and 2028–2029 regulations. The earlier curriculum applies to earlier entrants.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht’s Dutch-taught Health Sciences programme studies how biology, behaviour and the environment shape health. Its renewed curriculum combines thematic blocks, projects and learning in research, communication, collaboration and professional practice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The verified curriculum below includes the full first year and the third-year minor. A complete comparison awaits the detailed second-year curriculum and final-year graduation requirements for the renewed programme.

curriculum.limitation: 90 of 180 EC are verified for September 2026 entrants. Maastricht has reserved the detailed examination components for years two and three for later regulations.

componentNotes.y1-researcher: The four learning lines are integrated into the thematic blocks and projects. Their credits are shown separately in the regulations.
componentNotes.y3-minor: The curriculum reserves 30 EC for approved minor study. A minor outside the faculty requires prior approval.
componentNotes.y1-professional: The first-year programme requires satisfactory completion of all three thematic blocks, three projects and four learning lines. Attendance, active participation and the learning-line portfolio are assessed under the first-year rules.

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: is the gateway to UCR's biomedical/life-science cluster, a concrete complementary foundation for the biological determinants of health

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Measures disease burden and risk and studies epidemiological designs, bias and population prevention.

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Law, Society & Justice
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: examines legal, social and normative perspectives on justice and social problems, a concrete complementary contribution to both the policy/governance organisation of population health and the legal framing of health-system and environmental governance

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Climate Change
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: examines the physical science and societal consequences of climate change, directly implementing both the international/climate dimension of population health and the climate-resilience dimension of sustainable health systems

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Personal & Professional Development
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Required academic writing, research-question framing and reflective collaborative practice.

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Research Methods & Statistics
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Research design, surveys, sampling, statistical inference and regression support the evidenced research competency and data-analysis interests; no separate matched Maastricht module is asserted.
provisionalCourseFacts.priorContribution: is the gateway to UCR's quantitative research-methods cluster, directly implementing the programme's own introductory research-methods training

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Foundational brain, behaviour, learning and social influence before the applied health psychology course.

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Introduction to Data Science
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Data cleaning, integration, exploratory analysis and visualisation support the programme’s research/data interests; later-year methods content and weight remain unverified.
provisionalCourseFacts.priorContribution: develops data-cleaning, visualisation and manipulation skills, directly implementing the programme's own introductory data-analysis training

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Human Physiology
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: examines the structure and function of the human body's organ systems, a concrete complementary contribution to the biological foundations of health and disease

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Medical & Health Psychology
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Studies health inequalities, behaviour-change models and prevention through biopsychosocial research and applied cases.

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Introduction to Sociology
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: introduces the core sociological toolkit for analysing societies, a concrete complementary contribution to both the social organisation of care and the social integration of sustainable health systems

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: compares political systems and the institutions responsible for organising public services, a concrete complementary contribution to both public-health-policy governance and sustainability governance

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Public Economics
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: examines the rationale for government intervention and the efficiency/equity trade-offs of public funding, a concrete complementary contribution to health-policy funding and to the financing of sustainable, climate-resilient health infrastructure

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Infection & Immunity
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: examines host-pathogen interactions and the adaptive immune response to infection, a concrete complementary contribution to the biological-determinants-of-health basis

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Qualitative research questions, interviewing, observation, coding and reflexivity support the evidenced public-health research interest, without asserting a specific compulsory Maastricht qualitative-methods unit.
provisionalCourseFacts.priorContribution: trains qualitative research design and analysis, directly implementing the programme's own qualitative-research component

provisionalCourseFacts.name: Social Psychology
provisionalCourseFacts.contribution: Social cognition, attitudes, group processes and interpersonal behaviour supply a direct response to the evidenced behavioural determinants and social-norms interests, without claiming an identical Maastricht course.
